# Startup compatibility observations

Reference: unchanged Gophish Community Edition 0.12.1, commit 95618469799295e2c0fec980805a2dfbb818816b. tools/startup_capture/main.go belongs to the separate rewrite tooling and calls the exported config.LoadConfig and util.CheckAndCreateSSL functions without editing the reference. config.json was captured on 2026-10-18 and includes the original TestLoadConfig valid example plus defaults, duplicate/case-folded fields, nested merges, nulls, unknown fields, invalid types and trailing JSON. Expected values come from Go rather than the Rust decoder. Nil versus empty Go slices are equivalent for these configuration policies; the regression normalizes only that distinction.

go-admin.crt and go-admin.key are a synthetic P-384 certificate and SEC1 EC private key produced by Go's unchanged certificate helper. That legacy certificate has no SAN, so its one loopback compatibility request explicitly skips identity validation. go-rsa.crt and go-rsa.key were generated by the capture tool using Go's crypto/x509 and crypto/rsa, with a loopback SAN and PKCS#1 private key. Their TLS test validates the certificate using an explicit trusted root. All private keys here are deliberately public synthetic fixtures and must never be used for an installation.

The capture refuses an existing output directory. To extend it, capture into a new directory, review the observations, and copy only deliberately added fixtures; do not regenerate existing expectations silently. manifest.json records the reviewed bytes. Product tests use these files without requiring Go, Python, or the parent reference tree.

cli.json derives from tools/capture_cli.py --extended running the actual unchanged Go executable. It preserves observed exits, output-stream presence and whether parsing reached configuration loading; only the temporary missing-config filename is normalized. The negative boolean alias is --no-disable-mailer; explicit values such as --disable-mailer=false are rejected. Version output precedes a later unknown flag, whereas help does not hide unknown flags. The raw observation and compiler metadata remain in root docs/startup/cli-extended.json.
